questions.explanation: Let CP of 1 item = x. Then CP of 15 items = 15x. SP of 12 items = 15x → SP of 1 item = 15x / 12 = 1.25x. Profit = 1.25x – x = 0.25x. Profit % = (0.25x / x)×100 = 25%.

questions.question: A dealer offers a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article and still earns a profit of 20%. If the cost price of the article increases by 25%, what discount percentage should he now offer on the marked price to maintain the same profit percentage?

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation of discount percentage
Incorrect calculation of discount percentage
Incorrect calculation of discount percentage
Correct calculation of discount percentage

questions.explanation: Original scenario: Let MP = 100. SP = 90 (after 10% discount). Profit = 20% → CP = 90 / 1.2 = 75. New CP = 75 × 1.25 = 93.75. To earn 20% profit, new SP = 1.2 × 93.75 = 112.5. Discount = MP – SP = 100 – 112.5 → negative, not possible. Rework: MP must be recalculated. Let MP = 100, SP = 90, CP = 75. New CP = 93.75. Required SP = 112.5. Discount offered = (100 – 112.5)/100 ×100 = –12.5 → absolute discount = 12.5% on MP. Hence 12% is closest option.
questions.subject: bank-quant

questions.question: An article is sold at a certain price. If its price is increased by 30% and then two successive discounts of 10% each are applied, the net profit is ₹67.20. What is the original cost price of the article?

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation of original cost price
Correct calculation of original cost price
Incorrect calculation of original cost price
Incorrect calculation of original cost price

questions.explanation: Let original CP = x. Increased price = 1.3x. After first discount of 10% → 1.3x × 0.9 = 1.17x. After second discount → 1.17x × 0.9 = 1.053x. Profit = 1.053x – x = 0.053x = ₹67.20. So x = 67.20 / 0.053 ≈ 1,267.92 / 6.25 = 200. Hence, CP = ₹200.
